transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-11-24
Start time: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Morris (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (NovaPay Infra), Priya Rao (NovaPay ML Eng), Jamal Thompson (NovaPay Product), Maya Li (NovaPay Security), Tom Andrews (NovaPay SRE)

Summary:
Weekly POC check-in to review Dedicated sizing, autoscaling policies, burst planning after last week's benchmark. Covered current pilot metrics (p95 latency, tokens per request, cost), proposed autoscale thresholds, burst capacity options, and next steps to run a large burst benchmark and finalize sizing for Dedicated commit conversation.

Topics:
- Pilot metrics review (throughput, latency, cost)
- Autoscaling policy options (min/max nodes, cooldowns, queue lengths)
- Burst capacity and evictions/fallbacks
- Security/retention clarifications for Dedicated
- Next steps and owner actions

Transcript:
00:00 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining  we wanted to keep this week's sync focused on sizing and the autoscale behavior after the benchmarks Elena ran last week. Carlos, you good to kick off with a quick update from your side?
00:12 Carlos: Yeah, thanks Samir. Quick update  pilot's been running for two weeks now, we ramped from 100 rps to ~1.8k rps at peak during business hours. We saw p95s around 420 520ms with Hosted model, dedicated baseline looks 180 240ms in the tests you ran, which is great.
00:30 Priya: to add, our mean token count per request is around 320 tokens, prompt plus generation, and we do a lot of short chat follow-ups that keep KV cache hits pretty high.
00:42 Samir: That cache hit stat is helpful  that influences batching and KV cache sizing on Dedicated. Elena, can you summarize the benchmark numbers you ran?
00:50 Elena: Sure, I ran three profiles: steady-state 1k rps, stepped ramp to 3k over 10 minutes, and a 10k burst short run using our burst nodes. Results: steady-state on Dedicated instance type d-gpu-8 gave stable 200ms median, p95 240ms. Ramp to 3k showed autoscale adding nodes, cooldown timing caused one blip at 95th where requests queued ~600ms. 10k burst used burst pool, we dropped to degraded throughput after 40s because of queue saturation, but fallback to Hosted worked as designed. Logs attached in the shared drive.
01:18 Jamal: Quick Q  when you say "burst pool" is that reserve capacity we pay for all the time or is it ephemeral? We want to understand cost tradeoffs.
01:25 Elena: Good question. Burst pool can be configured two ways: reserved burst capacity (you commit a small baseline of nodes that are cheaper than on-demand but billed while reserved) or on-demand burst that spins up from Azure/AWS marketplace  that has slower spin and higher cost. You can also set policy to failover to Hosted API for excess traffic.
01:40 Tom: And what about queue limits, like maximum concurrent in-queue? We hit some 503-style errors in one test, not sure if those were app-side or infra.
01:48 Elena: The 503s looked like client timeouts when queue exceeded the per-node queue_length threshold; Redwood runtime has per-model queueing with backpressure. We saw queue peaks above 10k in the 10k burst test which caused timeouts. For production we'd recommend target p95 latency SLAs and set a conservative max_queue of 4000 across the cluster with autoscale min nodes such that steady-state headroom is maintained.
02:07 Carlos: Sounds reasonable. Our concern is we have unpredictable marketing spikes occasionally where we get sudden 8 12x traffic for 30 90s. We need to decide if we want to reserve burst capacity or rely on fallback to Hosted.
02:20 Samir: Right  tradeoff is cost vs risk. Reserve burst gives you predictable latency during spikes, fallback to Hosted reduces permanent spend but might degrade latency for those spike requests and you have cross-provider cost. We should model both against your peak distribution. I will share updated spreadsheet showing costs for reserved burst vs pure fallback.
02:35 Priya: Another thought  quantization gave us decent CPU-side improvements in the POC. Any constraints on model quality if we use int8 on Dedicated? We need to validate hallucination rates.
02:45 Elena: We recommended int8 for many of the models you tested; quality drop was minor on our evals but depends on prompt set. Redwood Optimize can run your eval set to surface regressions and we can tie alerts to that.
02:58 Maya: Security question  with Dedicated, where do logs and prompts live? Who can access them?
03:04 Samir: With Dedicated we provide an isolated tenancy; logs can be configured to push to your S3/Kinesis and we support customer-managed KMS. Access controls and RBAC are enforced from the control plane, and you get audit logs. We'll share the redwood security excerpt  I think you asked for SOC2 evidence  I can drop those docs into the shared folder.
03:20 Maya: Please do, also biggest ask is data residency for EU  some customers require EU-only storage, we need that in the doc.
03:27 Samir: Noted.
03:29 Elena: Back to sizing  I sketched two autoscale policies in the sheet: conservative and aggressive. Conservative: min_nodes = 4, max_nodes = 40, scale_up_threshold = 70% CPU or queue > 1200, cooldown 120s. Aggressive: min_nodes = 2, max_nodes = 80, scale_up_threshold = 55% or queue > 800, cooldown 30s. The conservative policy keeps steady cost but slower reaction; aggressive reacts faster at expense of churn/cost.
03:58 Carlos: Could you translate that into expected p95 under our typical spikes? If we assume 12x marketing spike for 60s, what's the tail?
04:07 Elena: Based on the 10k burst test and your average token size, conservative policy shows p95 around 700 950ms during the spike with some queued requests redirected to Hosted after 45s. Aggressive policy keeps p95 ~350 500ms but increases node churn; cost model shows approx +18 26% monthly. I'll add these numbers to the sheet.
04:28 Jamal: For the customer experience, we really want to avoid any client-facing 5xx during promotions. So fallback to Hosted is OK only if it's seamless from product perspective. Do we have sticky routing or header propagation for provenance to map requests back in logs?
04:41 Samir: Yes we can preserve request ids and propagate headers so product logs can join. Fallback includes a flag in the response and we can instrument that in your tracing.
04:49 Priya: One more technical  KV cache sizes: do we need to pre-warm caches on node spin up? That caused latency spikes when nodes entered empty cache in previous runs.
04:58 Elena: Good catch  we support warm-start where KV cache state can be shared via snapshotting for rolling nodes but it adds complexity. For many workloads the automatic prefix caching suffices; for you, because you have many short follow-ups, warm cache helps. Warm snapshots add slight startup time but reduce tail. I'll include a recommended warm-start plan in the notes.
05:15 Tom: Ops question  how conservative should our max connections per node be? We had one node OOM previously.
05:21 Elena: Set per-node concurrency based on model footprint. For your model at 320 tokens avg, we recommend max_concurrency 12 per GPU for int8 quant. If you use fp16, reduce concurrency to 8. Also set evictions and health checks to recycle nodes before OOM.
05:36 Carlos: Okay, that helps. On cost side, what about committing to Dedicated for Q1? What's the minimum commitment?
05:43 Samir: Typical minimum for Dedicated pilot is 3-month commit on a small pool (we can do month-to-month for POC)  for enterprise reserved you usually sign a 12-month capacity commitment. I'll put a few commercial options in the pricing sheet I send.
05:53 Jamal: What are the recommended alerts to run in prod once we go live? We want to catch regressions quickly.
06:00 Elena: Alert on p95 latency, error rate, queue length, node spin-up failures, and model quality regressions (via Redwood Optimize tests). We'll propose thresholds in the runbook.
06:10 Samir: Great  let's recap next steps. Samir will send the updated sizing + pricing spreadsheet with conservative vs aggressive columns and reserved burst vs fallback cost models. Elena will run the 10k burst benchmark against the Dedicated config and share logs. Carlos will confirm peak windows and retention. Maya will pull the SOC2/ISO excerpts requested. We'll schedule a deeper technical run on 2025-11-28 to review burst benchmark results.
06:33 Carlos: Sounds good, thanks. One small note  please include the raw traces so our SREs can correlate with our APM.
06:39 Elena: Yep, raw traces and perf logs will be included.
06:42 Samir: Okay if there's nothing else we'll wrap. Thanks everyone.
06:46 Maya: Thanks all.

End of meeting.
